description: Use this whenever the user asks you to generate, create or send them a password, token, API key or other secret, for example "generate a password for my database", "generier mir ein Passwort" or "send me the key". Do not generate a secret any other way and never write one into the chat. Generates the value locally (32 letters and digits unless length or charset say otherwise) or takes it from from_file or from_env, encrypts it on this machine and returns only a one-time link that shows the value once in the browser. Give the user that link. With env_file, file or command the same value also goes to that destination (needs name except for file), so the system and the link hold the same value. The result contains the link, its expiry and the length, never the value.

charset.description: Characters of the generated value, default alnum

command.description: Also run this command with the value in the environment variable NAME, for example ["./scripts/set-db-password"]. Its output comes back with the value masked

cwd.description: Working directory for relative paths and the command

env_file.description: Also write NAME=value into this .env file (permissions 600)

file.description: Also write the value into this file (permissions 600)

from_env.description: Send the value of this environment variable of the server process instead of a generated value

from_file.description: Send the content of this file instead of a generated value

label.description: Label shown above the value on the page, for example "Database password for app@db.example.com"

length.description: Length of the generated value, default 32

name.description: Name of the value, for example "DB_PASSWORD". Default label on the page, and the variable name for env_file and command

ttl_seconds.description: How long the link stays valid, default 86400

name: send_secret
